gaps.sentence: 'I'm exhausted,' she said. She said she ___ exhausted.
gaps.explanation: Present simple/progressive shifts to past in reported speech: am → was.

gaps.sentence: 'I have to catch the last train,' she said. She said she ___ catch the last train.
gaps.explanation: Have to (obligation) backshifts to had to after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: 'Shall I close the window?' he asked. He asked ___ close the window.
gaps.explanation: Shall I...? (offering) becomes if/whether he should... in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'Please don't leave until the lights are off,' the caretaker begged us. The caretaker begged ___ until the lights were off.
gaps.explanation: Begging somebody not to do something uses object + not to + infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'Where do you live?' he asked me. He asked me where I ___.
gaps.explanation: Reported questions use statement word order, and present simple backshifts: do you live → I lived.

gaps.sentence: 'You should apply for the grant,' he told me. He ___ me to apply for the grant.
gaps.explanation: Advice is reported as advise + object + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'Why hasn't she replied?' he wondered. He wondered why she ___ replied.
gaps.explanation: hasn't replied → hadn't replied: statement order and past perfect.

gaps.sentence: 'Would you like to stay for dinner?' they asked. They ___ me to stay for dinner.
gaps.explanation: Offers of this kind are reported as invited somebody to do something.
